items.q: Having spent a decade on the novel, she was ______ when every publisher rejected it and did not write another word for years.
items.vi: Sau khi dành cả một thập kỷ cho cuốn tiểu thuyết, bà đã vô cùng đau khổ khi mọi nhà xuất bản đều từ chối nó và suốt nhiều năm không viết thêm một chữ nào.
items.explanation: Meaning: every publisher rejected it and she did not write another word for years — deep, lasting unhappiness, so disconsolate (too sad to be comforted). ✗ complacent — smugly satisfied, the opposite of crushed; ✗ nonchalant — calmly unconcerned, but she stopped writing for years; ✗ euphoric — intensely happy, impossible after total rejection.

items.q: Wind and solar now ______ almost a third of the country's demand for electricity on a typical summer afternoon.
items.vi: Điện gió và điện mặt trời hiện đáp ứng gần một phần ba nhu cầu điện của cả nước vào một buổi chiều mùa hè điển hình.
items.explanation: Collocation: the object is demand for electricity, and the verb that goes with demand is meet (meet the demand = supply what is needed). ✗ reach — you reach a target, a level or a figure, not a demand; ✗ fill — you fill a gap, a vacancy or an order, not a demand; ✗ answer — you answer a question, a call or a need; 'answer demand for electricity' is not standard.

items.q: The festival lost money this year, but as its director put it, there is no use ______ when next summer's programme still has to be planned.
items.vi: Liên hoan năm nay bị lỗ, nhưng như giám đốc nói, than khóc chuyện đã rồi cũng chẳng ích gì khi chương trình mùa hè năm sau vẫn còn phải lên kế hoạch.
items.explanation: Idiom: the festival lost money (done, cannot be changed) and next year still has to be planned, so regretting the past is pointless — crying over spilt milk (wasting time on what cannot be undone). ✗ beating about the bush — avoiding the main point; ✗ burning the midnight oil — working very late; ✗ sitting on the fence — refusing to take sides.

items.q: ______ the engineers suspect that the bridge's cables had been corroding for years when they signed off the routine inspection report.
items.vi: Các kỹ sư hầu như không hề ngờ rằng dây cáp của cây cầu đã bị ăn mòn suốt nhiều năm khi họ ký duyệt báo cáo kiểm tra định kỳ.
items.explanation: Inversion after a fronted negative: Little (= not at all) is followed by auxiliary + subject + bare verb, and the bare verb suspect fits Little did the engineers suspect. ✗ Hardly had — needs a past participle (had suspected) and a later 'when' for the next event; ✗ Not until — opens a time clause in normal order and puts the inversion in a main clause, which this sentence lacks; ✗ Only when — same problem: the inversion belongs in the main clause, not right after it.

items.q: With borrowing costs rising sharply, the utility has ______ its plans for a second offshore wind farm to a fraction of the original size.
items.vi: Do chi phí vay tăng mạnh, công ty điện lực đã thu hẹp kế hoạch xây trang trại điện gió ngoài khơi thứ hai xuống chỉ còn một phần nhỏ so với quy mô ban đầu.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: the clue is to a fraction of the original size — the plans were reduced, so scaled back (cut down in size or scope). ✗ scaled up — increased, the opposite of the clue; ✗ brought back — reintroduced or returned; nothing is being revived here; ✗ fallen back — retreated or dropped behind, and it takes no direct object, but 'its plans' follows the blank.

items.q: The reviewer ______ the whole novel; her summary gets the ending completely wrong.
items.vi: Nhà phê bình chắc chắn đã không đọc hết cuốn tiểu thuyết; bản tóm tắt của bà ấy sai hoàn toàn về đoạn kết.
items.explanation: Modal deduction about the past: the summary gets the ending completely wrong, so the speaker is sure she did NOT read it all — a confident negative deduction is can't have + past participle. ✗ needn't have read — she read it but it was unnecessary, not the point; ✗ shouldn't have read — a criticism of something she did, not a deduction; ✗ mustn't have read — must have is used for positive deduction only; its negative is can't have.

items.q: Local investors remain ______ about the new pipeline, fearing that a single leak could wipe out years of returns.
items.vi: Các nhà đầu tư địa phương vẫn lo ngại về đường ống mới, e rằng chỉ một vụ rò rỉ cũng có thể xóa sạch lợi nhuận của nhiều năm.
items.explanation: Meaning: fearing that a single leak could wipe out years of returns is worry about a possible future harm, so apprehensive (anxious that something bad may happen). ✗ jubilant — triumphantly happy, clashing with 'fearing'; ✗ nostalgic — longing for the past, nothing to do with a future leak; ✗ resentful — bitter about a wrong already done, but no harm has happened yet.

items.q: The conductor was determined to ______ the restoration of the concert hall ______, however long the fundraising took.
items.vi: Vị nhạc trưởng quyết tâm theo đuổi việc trùng tu nhà hát hòa nhạc đến cùng, dù việc gây quỹ có kéo dài bao lâu.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: determined and however long the fundraising took mean continuing until the restoration is finished — see something through. ✗ look / through — look through means examine or read quickly, not persist; ✗ see / off — see off means say goodbye to someone or chase away, not complete a project; ✗ see / into — see into means look inside or perceive (see into the future), not finish.

items.q: The safety board recommended that the ageing reactor ______ offline until every crack in the cooling system had been examined.
items.vi: Ủy ban an toàn khuyến nghị rằng lò phản ứng cũ kỹ phải được ngừng hoạt động cho đến khi mọi vết nứt trong hệ thống làm mát được kiểm tra.
items.explanation: Subjunctive after a verb of recommending: recommended that is followed by the base form, with no tense or agreement, so be taken. ✗ was taken — past indicative; a recommendation says what should happen, not what happened; ✗ is taken — present indicative, and it also clashes with past 'recommended'; ✗ would be taken — would belongs to predictions and conditionals, not the that-clause after recommend.

items.q: When the boy insisted he had not meant to break the vase, his mother chose to ______ rather than punish him.
options: give him a piece of her mind
give him the benefit of the doubt
give him a run for his money
items.answer: give him the benefit of the doubt
items.vi: Khi cậu bé khăng khăng rằng mình không cố ý làm vỡ bình hoa, mẹ cậu quyết định tin lời cậu thay vì phạt cậu.
items.explanation: Idiom: the mother chose to believe him rather than punish him, so she gave him the benefit of the doubt (accepted his word without proof). ✗ give him a piece of her mind — an angry telling-off, the opposite of not punishing; ✗ give him the cold shoulder — deliberate unfriendliness, itself a punishment; ✗ give him a run for his money — strong competition, meaningless between a mother and a small boy.

items.q: Several critics ______ the charge of plagiarism at the young novelist, though none produced a single copied sentence.
items.vi: Nhiều nhà phê bình đã buộc tội nhà tiểu thuyết trẻ đạo văn, dù không ai đưa ra được một câu sao chép nào.
items.explanation: Collocation: the noun is the charge of plagiarism, and the verb for aiming an accusation at someone is level (level a charge / an accusation / criticism at). ✗ threw — you throw a ball or a punch; 'throw a charge at' is not standard; ✗ pointed — you point a finger or a gun at someone, not a charge; ✗ sent — you send a letter or a message, and send does not take 'at'.

items.q: ______, the rescue helicopters will resume their search of the northern slopes at first light tomorrow.
items.vi: Nếu thời tiết cho phép, các trực thăng cứu hộ sẽ nối lại việc tìm kiếm trên các sườn núi phía bắc vào lúc rạng sáng mai.
items.explanation: Absolute participle clause: Weather permitting = if the weather permits; the weather is the doer of 'permit', so the present (active) participle is needed. ✗ Weather permitted — a past participle is passive, making the weather the thing permitted; ✗ Weather to permit — an infinitive does not form an absolute clause; ✗ Weather having permitted — the perfect participle describes a condition already met, but the search is tomorrow.

items.q: After the fourth blackout in a single week, residents were ______, and dozens wrote to the newspapers demanding that the grid operator resign.
items.vi: Sau lần mất điện thứ tư chỉ trong một tuần, cư dân vô cùng bực tức, và hàng chục người đã viết thư cho báo chí yêu cầu đơn vị vận hành lưới điện từ chức.
items.explanation: Meaning: the fourth blackout in a single week and letters demanding that the grid operator resign show anger after repeated annoyance — exasperated (extremely irritated). ✗ serene — calm and peaceful, contradicting the angry letters; ✗ gratified — pleased and satisfied; nobody is pleased by four blackouts; ✗ apathetic — uninterested, but dozens bothered to write and demand a resignation.

items.q: Most participants denied ______ the instructions, even though the recording showed them reading the page twice.
items.vi: Hầu hết người tham gia phủ nhận đã đọc hướng dẫn, dù đoạn ghi hình cho thấy họ đọc trang đó hai lần.
items.explanation: Verb pattern: deny takes a gerund (-ing), never a to-infinitive, and the perfect gerund having read marks the reading as earlier than the denying (the recording shows it already happened). ✗ to read — a to-infinitive, not used after deny; ✗ to have read — a perfect infinitive, still an infinitive, so not used after deny; ✗ read — a bare verb cannot follow deny; 'denied read' is ungrammatical.

items.q: The appeal court ______ the verdict after new evidence showed that the key witness had lied under oath.
items.vi: Tòa phúc thẩm đã hủy bản án sau khi bằng chứng mới cho thấy nhân chứng chủ chốt đã khai man khi tuyên thệ.
items.explanation: Phrasal verb: an appeal court acting on new evidence cancels an earlier verdict — the legal term is set aside (annul, declare invalid). ✗ set about — begin a task or attack someone; a court does not begin a verdict; ✗ set out — start a journey or state something clearly; ✗ set off — depart or trigger (an alarm, an explosion), not cancel.

items.q: The city's grid was designed for half its present population; ______, blackouts have become a routine feature of every heatwave.
items.vi: Lưới điện của thành phố được thiết kế cho một nửa dân số hiện tại; do đó, mất điện đã trở thành chuyện thường lệ trong mỗi đợt nắng nóng.
items.explanation: Linking adverb: the grid was built for half its present population, and routine blackouts are the result, so consequently. ✗ nevertheless — signals contrast ('despite that'), but the second clause follows from the first, not against it; ✗ otherwise — means 'if not', describing what would happen if the first clause were untrue; ✗ moreover — simply adds another point, without showing that the blackouts are caused by the undersized grid.

items.q: Nurses who ______ for their patients report higher job satisfaction, the study found, even though they work longer hours.
items.vi: Nghiên cứu cho thấy những y tá nỗ lực hết mình vì bệnh nhân có mức độ hài lòng với công việc cao hơn, dù họ làm việc nhiều giờ hơn.
items.explanation: Idiom: higher job satisfaction... even though they work longer hours describes nurses who make extra effort — go the extra mile (do more than is expected). ✗ go through the roof — rise very fast (prices) or lose one's temper; ✗ go with the flow — accept whatever happens without effort, the opposite of extra effort; ✗ go round in circles — make no progress, and it cannot take 'for their patients'.

items.q: Neither the playwright nor the actors ______ willing to comment on the cancelled tour when the press arrived.
items.vi: Cả nhà viết kịch lẫn các diễn viên đều không muốn bình luận về chuyến lưu diễn bị hủy khi báo chí đến.
items.explanation: Agreement with neither... nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the actors (plural), and when the press arrived sets the time in the past, so were. ✗ was — singular, agreeing with 'the playwright', the further subject; ✗ is — singular and present, wrong on both counts; ✗ has been — singular and present perfect, while the sentence describes one past moment.

items.q: He was ______ to discover that he had sent the unfinished draft, complete with his private notes, to the entire faculty.
items.vi: Anh ta vô cùng xấu hổ khi phát hiện ra mình đã gửi bản thảo chưa hoàn thành, kèm cả những ghi chú riêng tư, cho toàn bộ khoa.
items.explanation: Meaning: sending an unfinished draft complete with his private notes to the entire faculty is a humiliating mistake, so mortified (extremely embarrassed). ✗ overjoyed — delighted, the opposite reaction; ✗ appeased — calmed after being angry, but nothing had made him angry; ✗ vindicated — proved right after doubt, but the discovery proves a blunder, not a point.

items.q: To ______ the ball ______, the moderator asked each panellist to name one film that had changed their mind about something.
items.vi: Để khởi động buổi thảo luận, người điều phối đề nghị mỗi khách mời kể tên một bộ phim đã làm thay đổi suy nghĩ của họ về điều gì đó.
items.explanation: Fixed idiom: get the ball rolling = start something happening, matching the moderator's opening question. ✗ put / rolling — put is not the verb of this idiom (get or set the ball rolling); ✗ get / running — 'get something running' works for an engine, but the ball idiom needs rolling; ✗ make / turning — neither word belongs to the idiom, and 'make the ball turning' is ungrammatical (make takes a bare infinitive, not -ing).

items.q: ______ a community feels about the reliability of its power supply, the less willing it is to oppose new pylons nearby.
items.vi: Một cộng đồng càng lo lắng về độ tin cậy của nguồn điện thì càng ít muốn phản đối việc dựng cột điện mới gần đó.
items.explanation: Double comparative: the less willing in the second half signals the pattern 'the + comparative..., the + comparative...', so the first half must be The more anxious. ✗ The most anxious — a superlative; the pattern needs a comparative; ✗ More anxious — a comparative without 'the', which the paired structure requires; ✗ The much anxious — 'much anxious' is not a comparative at all (much modifies comparatives: much more anxious).

items.q: Researchers are careful to ______ a distinction between a habit, which is automatic, and an addiction, which persists despite harm.
items.vi: Các nhà nghiên cứu cẩn thận phân biệt giữa thói quen, vốn mang tính tự động, và chứng nghiện, vốn tồn tại dai dẳng bất chấp tác hại.
items.explanation: Collocation: the noun is a distinction between two things, and the verbs that go with it are draw or make; only draw is offered. ✗ put — put goes with 'a question' or 'a case', not a distinction; ✗ take — take goes with 'a decision' or 'a view', not a distinction; ✗ set — set goes with 'a limit' or 'a standard'; 'set a distinction' is not English.

items.q: 'What if the grant runs out before the survey is finished?' 'It may never happen, so let's ______.'
options: cross that bridge when we come to it
items.answer: cross that bridge when we come to it
items.vi: 'Nếu khoản tài trợ cạn trước khi cuộc khảo sát hoàn thành thì sao?' 'Chuyện đó có thể chẳng bao giờ xảy ra, nên đến lúc đó rồi tính.'
items.explanation: Idiom: It may never happen — the problem is only possible, so deal with it if and when it arises: cross that bridge when we come to it. ✗ burn our bridges — destroy any way back, an irreversible act; ✗ bite the bullet — face something unpleasant now, the opposite of waiting; ✗ let sleeping dogs lie — avoid stirring up an old problem, but this problem lies in the future, not the past.

items.q: By the time the new dam is completed, an estimated forty villages ______ to higher ground by the authorities.
items.vi: Đến khi con đập mới hoàn thành, ước tính khoảng bốn mươi ngôi làng sẽ đã được chính quyền di dời lên vùng đất cao hơn.
items.explanation: Tense and voice: By the time the new dam is completed points to an action finished before a future moment (future perfect), and by the authorities names the agent, so the passive is needed: will have been moved. ✗ will have moved — future perfect but active, so the villages would be doing the moving, clashing with 'by the authorities'; ✗ will be moving — future continuous, an action in progress, not completed; ✗ have been moving — present perfect continuous, active and not future.

items.q: The finding that participants who were paid more performed worse left the psychologists ______, as it contradicted every existing model of motivation.
items.vi: Phát hiện rằng những người tham gia được trả nhiều tiền hơn lại làm việc kém hơn khiến các nhà tâm lý học bối rối, vì nó mâu thuẫn với mọi mô hình động lực hiện có.
items.explanation: Meaning: the result contradicted every existing model, so the psychologists could not explain it — perplexed (confused, puzzled). ✗ reassured — comforted, feeling less worried; an unexplained result does the opposite; ✗ smug — self-satisfied, which fits confirmed models, not overturned ones; ✗ remorseful — sorry for a wrong done, but the psychologists did nothing wrong.
